message: Command `cd /workspace && bash build.sh 'sed -n "260,340p" /gt/_work/build-asan-internal/_deps/deflate-src/lib/deflate_decompress.c'` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
So `ZLIB_MIN_OVERHEAD = 6`. The check `in_nbytes < 6` returns BAD_DATA. So `get_unaligned_be16(in_next)` at line 49 reads 2 bytes, which is safe since in_nbytes >= 6. 

The real overread is in the DEFLATE decompression. The `REFILL_BITS_BRANCHLESS()` reads a full machine word (8 bytes on 64-bit) from `in_next`. When the input is near the end, this can overread past the end of the buffer. But the `REFILL_BITS()` macro checks `in_end - in_next >= sizeof(bitbuf_t)` before using the branchless method, so it falls back to byte-at-a-time near the end.

However, the `REFILL_BITS_IN_FASTLOOP()` doesn't check for end of input. Let me look at that.
